fact.perry-statue: Late in life, on a trip to Russia, Fred Perry was shown a spy satellite photo of the Wimbledon grounds by an ex-KGB man. He pointed out Perry's own statue in it.
fact.caesars-camp: Under a golf course on Wimbledon Common lies Caesar's Camp, an Iron Age hill fort more than 2,000 years old. In 1875 the landowner had it flattened.
fact.st-helier-alphabet: The St Helier estate's roads run in alphabetical order, from one corner of the estate to Woburn Road at the other.
fact.hartley-fireproof: David Hartley invented fireproof plates and built a fireproof house on Putney Heath. Its lower floor was set on fire again and again, with George III and Queen Charlotte watching.
fact.putney-duel: In September 1809 two Cabinet ministers, George Canning and Lord Castlereagh, fought a duel on Putney Heath, near where the Telegraph pub is now.
fact.tutankhamun-putney: Howard Carter, the archaeologist who found Tutankhamun's tomb in Egypt, is buried at Putney Vale Cemetery.
fact.old-rectory: In December 1546, near the end of his life, Henry VIII was too ill to get back to Whitehall. He stopped at Wimbledon's Old Rectory and stayed three days.
fact.selassie-cannizaro: Haile Selassie, emperor of Ethiopia, stayed in Wimbledon in 1936 after Italy invaded his country and he was forced into exile.
fact.snuff-mills: The two old watermills in Morden Hall Park were used to grind tobacco into snuff, the powdered tobacco people sniffed.
